chunks: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever holds God in such reverence that he does not swear by Him, God gives him better than what would have gone from him.

key_terms.أجل: To hold in reverence, to deem too great or exalted; here: treating God as too exalted to be invoked in a casual oath
key_terms.خير: Good, better; in the context of divine reward, a superior worldly or spiritual alternative
key_terms.يحلف: To swear/take an oath; the verbal form here implies a prohibited or strongly discouraged action

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about not swearing by God out of reverence?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) taught that refraining from taking oaths in God's name out of reverence for the divine is itself rewarded by God. The believer who abstains from swearing by Allah — not due to weakness but out of deep veneration — will receive a divine compensation greater than whatever worldly benefit would have been secured by the oath. This teaching reflects the Shia legal and ethical tradition discouraging casual oaths, especially those invoking God's name.
